basics.name: Jason Hung
basics.label: Plant Operations Executive / Plant Manager
basics.summary: Manufacturing executive with 17+ years of experience across electronics manufacturing, quality, R&D and business operations. Former plant manager, management director and co-founder / executive vice president, with experience managing manufacturing organizations of more than 1,000 employees in Shanghai, Suzhou, Kunshan and Changshu. Integrates production, quality, engineering, EHS, HR and ESG to improve profitability, efficiency, delivery and talent development.

Advanced lean manufacturing through OEE, downtime and changeover management, with daily and weekly production reviews.
Led implementation, maintenance and audit preparation for ISO 9001, IATF 16949, ISO 14001 / 45001, QC 080000, TISAX, RBA and EcoVadis systems.
Served as SHE Manager with overall production safety responsibility, overseeing EHS risk controls, emergency drills and leadership development.
Directed engineering and intellectual property strategy, introducing an Engineering AI Agent to review patent gaps, competing technologies and design-around risks.
Participated in AI research on keycap pull-force prediction using material, opening dimensions and force data to explore design optimization and offline validation.

projects.name: AI Process & Engineering Parameter Optimization
projects.role: Participated in engineering pull-force prediction and supported manufacturing AI applications through plant management.
projects.summary: Translated manufacturing and design problems into measurable parameters, prediction targets and validation workflows. Studied key pressing, paint fixtures, pogo-pin force, keycap pull force and laser-engraving parameter optimization.
highlights: Pull-force prediction: the presentation explicitly lists Jason Hung as a participant. Material, opening dimensions and force data were explored to support design decisions and reduce trial and error.

Cross-functional case: the key-pressing project reported an offline experimental metric increasing from 200 to 1,113 pcs per operation. This is a team-reported result for a specific operation, not a whole-line capacity increase.
Implementation approach: connect shop-floor problems, data preparation, modeling, parameter recommendations and offline validation, distinguishing validated results from cost estimates.

details.title: Research Question & Method
details.text: The keycap pull-force project addressed hook-opening dimensions that relied on experience and tooling trials. It used material and historical force data to explore dimension prediction and parameter recommendations. The presentation records 20 modeling samples and 3 additional test samples: preliminary validation requiring more data across specifications and operating conditions.

details.title: Manufacturing Validation
details.text: The key-pressing case combined cylinder pressure, ejection time, pressing time and rubber hardness. Following model recommendations and offline testing, the team reported a metric increase from 200 to 1,113 pcs per operation. The original unit and limited scope are retained.

details.title: Benefits & Research Limitations
details.text: The pull-force project estimated RMB 104,800 per year across tooling modification, experimental labor and new-hire training. This is a scenario estimate, not realized savings, and is not added to the RMB 2M+ annual result in the resume. Further work includes tolerance recommendations, larger samples and continued offline validation.

projects.source: AI Project Optimization Summary, slides 20, 22, 62, 66–67, 71, 74 and 79–80. Named participation applies to the pull-force project; other cases summarize team reports.

projects.name: Jingtek E-bike App & IoT Service System
projects.category: Product Planning & Entrepreneurship Research | E-bike / IoT
projects.role: Draws on product development and App / administration architecture planning during the co-founder / executive vice president role.
projects.summary: Explored integration of e-bike hardware communications, mobile applications and administration systems, extending product capabilities into online transactions, after-sales services and user communities.
highlights: Scope included vehicle anomaly detection, repair locations, online shopping, member and product administration, and customer-behavior and sales analysis.
Planned community interaction, test rides and loyalty points to connect product services with market development.
Explored GPS positioning, rental geofencing, communication compatibility and OTA update requirements.

details.title: App & Administration Planning
details.text: The presentation covers vehicle anomaly detection, nearby repair locations, shopping, wish lists and points redemption. Administration includes member, product and maintenance management, plus customer-behavior and sales analysis, considering product development and after-sales workflows together.

details.title: IoT & Business Model Research
details.text: Explored community features, test rides and maintenance services to support engagement, alongside online transactions and experience sharing. Rental concepts proposed GPS, anti-theft and geofencing requirements; hardware planning included communication compatibility and an OTA update library.

details.title: Scope of Experience
details.text: This case demonstrates system planning, hardware–software integration and business model research. The presentation provides no revenue, user-count or full-launch validation, so proposed features are not presented as realized commercial results. Its requirement to support over 60% of communication protocols is a different metric from the resume’s over 65% hardware compatibility result.

projects.source: Jingtek E_bike app system, slides 3 and 5–16. Personal responsibilities are contextualized by the entrepreneurship and App architecture experience in the September 15 resume.

projects.name: Agentic Workflows & Manufacturing Governance
projects.role: Studied Morris Fan’s lecture materials to explore workflow integration and governance for private enterprise AI agents.
projects.summary: Used The Practice and Challenges of Agentic Workflows as a study reference, focusing on manufacturing problem definition, data and tool integration, human review and traceable decision processes.
highlights: Studied task decomposition, knowledge retrieval, tool execution, result validation and human review.
Examined ERP / MES / SCM integration, RAG, MCP, tool permissions, exception handling and audit trails.
Explored equipment troubleshooting, scheduling, demand forecasting and supply-chain early warning as application scenarios.

details.title: Architecture & Workflow Study
details.text: Reviewed the lecture’s data and tool layers, agent core, workflow orchestration and governance architecture. Explored turning operational needs into executable, observable tasks with clear boundaries for queries, tool actions and result verification.

details.title: Manufacturing Governance
details.text: Focused on human-in-the-loop review, tool permissions, evidence logs, exception handling and stop mechanisms. Considered irreversibility, production risk and data sensitivity, alongside task success rate, cost, latency and failure recovery.

details.title: Applications & Attribution
details.text: Equipment maintenance, quality knowledge, production scheduling, demand forecasting and supply-chain early warning are directions for further study. This is a review of lecture materials authored by Morris Fan; the lecture’s demonstration systems, code and results are not claimed as personal development or deployment outcomes.

projects.source: Morris Fan, The Practice and Challenges of Agentic Workflows, pages 4–13, 27–32, 73–82 and 84–91. Third-party study reference, not a personal publication.

projects.name: E-Vehicle Controller Embedded Development
projects.summary: Building on 10+ years of embedded development experience, ongoing firmware and tooling development for an e-bike controller (three-phase BLDC motor control): motor control algorithms, migration of production-proven protection logic, communication protocol design, Windows tuning tools and AI-assisted diagnostics over logged operating data.

details.title: Motor Control & Firmware
details.text: Re-implemented production-proven control logic on a modern dual-core MCU with integrated CAN/BLE: three-phase BLDC commutation and SVPWM sinusoidal control, overcurrent / undervoltage / stall protection, and firmware-level electromagnetic braking (E-ABS) with regenerative energy recovery and safety management.

details.title: Protocols & Toolchain
details.text: Designed serial communication protocols and debug frames (controller–display–BMS) and built a Windows tuning tool covering parameter read/write, Hall calibration, live charts and diagnostic export, supporting motor matching and production calibration.

details.title: AI Applications
details.text: Exported operating data (current, speed, voltage, load state) as structured diagnostic packages; explored LLM-assisted fault diagnosis and motor-parameter self-learning as a bridge to IoT services and after-sales applications.
